sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Statutory Company Secretarial and Commercial Registered Agent Office

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (Grand Duchy of Luxembourg) - unitary national jurisdiction without sub-state tax distinctions
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic family; Code civil, Code de commerce and Code monétaire et financier, with French and Belgian doctrinal influence; secondary sources include EU Regulations directly applicable in the national legal order)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: US-Luxembourg Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (in force 1964, as amended by the 1996 and 2009 amending Protocols)
EU-Singapore Investment Protection Agreement (applicable EU-level treaty provisionally applied from 21 November 2019 and entered into force for Luxembourg as an EU Member State on 14 February 2020)
Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) Bilateral Investment Treaty with the People's Republic of China (signed 2005, in force 1 April 2009)
Luxembourg-Hong Kong SAR Agreement for the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 1 November 2017, in force 2018)
Luxembourg-Germany Double Taxation Agreement (in force 1959, as amended by the 2012 amending Protocol)
Luxembourg-France Double Taxation Agreement (in force 1959, as amended, including the Protocol of 2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (including by the Laws of 21 July 2020 and 10 February 2022, transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended; Law of 11 February 2013 introducing the SCSp regime and the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT, as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 27 January 2020; CSSF Circulars 18/698 (tax offences), 19/759 (suspicious transaction reporting to the Cellule de Renseignement Financier - CRF) and the consolidated CSSF AML/CFT risk-based supervision framework; Law of 5 August 2019 on professionals of the financial sector.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (restricted public legitimate-interest access; following the Luxembourg Constitutional Court ruling of 17 November 2023, general public access to the RBE register has been curtailed. For an SCSp, the UBO declaration is lodged with the Luxembourg Business Registers and is accessible principally to the FIU (Cellule de Renseignement Financier - CRF), the CSSF, the Luxembourg tax administration (ACD), judicial authorities, and notaries/fiduciaries bound by professional confidentiality; SCSp beneficiaries additionally benefit from the specific confidentiality framework of Article 5(2) of the Law of 13 January 2019).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the valid passport of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) and of the General Partner's authorised signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing competent authority of the UBO's state of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille certification pursuant to the Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961 (Luxembourg is a Contracting Party; consular legalization required only for non-Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of tax residence (certificat de résidence) of each UBO and of the General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent tax authority of the UBO's country of fiscal residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Convention states; for non-Convention states, dual-side consular legalization by the Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate in the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original proof of physical residential address (utility bill or bank-confirmed address attestation) dated within three months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or a deposit-taking bank in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature path (apostille not standardly required for bank/utility evidence; notarization accepted by Luxembourg AML gatekeepers)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and company register extract (where a UBO is a corporate entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company register or registrar of the UBO corporate entity's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the state of incorporation, or consular legalization for non-Convention jurisdictions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening at onboarding of each UBO, the General Partner, all authorised signatories and professional counterparties against: (i) the CSSF consolidated sanctions lists and EU autonomous sanctions (Council Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 and implementing regulations; Council Regulation (EU) No 833/2014 as amended), (ii) UN Security Council consolidated lists, (iii) the OFAC SDN list, (iv) FATF and national PEP databases administered through the CRF, and (v) the Luxembourg domestic PEP list per Article 3(7) of the Law of 12 November 2004. Enhanced due diligence (source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation) is mandatory for all politically exposed persons and for counterparties resident in high-risk third countries identified by FATF and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/1675, as amended. Refresh screening is required at least annually, upon material adverse-media triggers, and upon any change of control or UBO composition.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS electronic portal at rcs.lbr.lu (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés de Luxembourg)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SCSp name must be drafted in Roman (Latin) script; French, German, or Luxembourgish are the official statutory drafting languages. Luxembourg law requires the SCSp name to contain the statutory designator 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale'. Foreign-language names must be transliterated to Latin script, must not be misleading, contrary to public policy (bonnes mœurs), or confusingly identical to an existing RCS-registered name. Name availability is evidenced through the RCS 'certificat de non-opposition' procedure.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Fonds d'investissement / Reserved Alternative Investment Fund / Fund
Luxembourg (as a leading standalone token without a distinct corporate discriminator)
Chambre de Commerce / Chamber of Commerce
S.A. / SA / S.à r.l. / SARL / SCS / SCA / SECS / SE (protected legal-form suffixes or misleading type designators reserved for entities of the corresponding statutory form)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon an RCS refusal of a proposed name, the applicant may within one month submit a corrective name request via rcs.lbr.lu, or request issuance of a fresh negative certificate for an alternative name. An administrative appeal lies before the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months of notification of the refusal under the general administrative procedure rules; a further appeal is available to the Administrative Court (Cour administrative). In practice, the LBR offers pre-submission name-consultation by email to reduce rejection risk, and after expiry of the 30-day negative-certificate window the certificate can be re-issued without prejudice to refile at the standard tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted permissibility. An SCSp must maintain a genuine registered office in Luxembourg under the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (SCSp rules introduced by the Law of 11 February 2013). Use of a CSSF-authorised third-party domiciliation agent (société de domiciliation under the Law of 5 August 2019 on professionals of the financial sector) is standard market practice and is expressly accepted. A bare virtual mailbox with no authorised Luxembourg domiciliary agent, no statutory-books presence, and no capacity to receive service of process is not permitted. For the regulated company-secretarial and commercial registered-agent activity (ISIC 8299), the operating entity must hold or operate under an appropriate CSSF authorisation; commercial substance principles (local management, Luxembourg bank account, local books and records, payroll/compliance function) must be maintained.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified at approximately 20% annual probability for an active regulated registered-agent and secretarial business (reflecting CSSF inspection prerogatives under the Law of 5 August 2019, ACD tax audit powers and ITIE/SSI social-security inspections); reduced to below 10% for a dormant or purely holding SCSp; unannounced on-site inspections are a recognised statutory mechanism and cannot be excluded.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS/LBR electronic name-clearance tariff (approximately EUR 32)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of the SCSp partnership deed (contrat de société) including UBO provisions, reserved decision-making matrix and confidentiality clauses
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent Luxembourg law firm admitted to the Luxembourg Bar
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for SCSp formation fixed-fee mandates (market range approximately EUR 1,500 to EUR 3,000; USD 2,200 planning midpoint)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notary certification of the partnership deed (required only where real estate or immovable rights are contributed; otherwise the private-deed path is available)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary public (Ordre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Luxembourg notarial fee schedule; statutory tariff estimate for a short-form SCSp deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Electronic filing and registration of the SCSp in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS electronic-submission filing tariff (approximately EUR 60)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation deed and statutory particulars in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RESA official electronic gazette
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RESA publication tariff dependent on deed length (approximately EUR 100)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration filing in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory no-fee regime for the initial UBO declaration (complimentary electronic filing)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / domiciliation services via a CSSF-authorised third-party domiciliation agent (first annual cycle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Luxembourg market benchmark for commercial domiciliation (approximately EUR 1,200 per annum)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT onboarding package - UBO piercing, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth review, PEP and OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening, and client risk scoring
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Outsourced AML compliance consultant / screening software provider engaged by the forming law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing compliance-market benchmark per entity file (enhanced due diligence package)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille legalization of foreign-issued UBO passport copies and certificates of tax residence (estimated two origin documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the UBO or certificate's state of issuance (foreign Ministry of Foreign Affairs or public registry)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing international apostille tariffs (approximately USD 50 to USD 70 per document)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, in particular Articles 1-14 (general company provisions), Articles 102-108 (limited partnerships) and the SCSp provisions introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016; supplemented by Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 September 2016 on registration in the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized or private partnership deed (contrat de société) of the SCSp accompanied by RCS registration application Form A
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for the SCSp and no escrow-account obligation; the partners freely determine the capital contributions and contribution schedule in the partnership deed, and contributions may be made in cash or in kind.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the partners hereby approve the partnership deed of [Company Name] SCSp and subscribe to the partnership interests as set out in Schedule 1. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [registered address], Luxembourg, and that the partnership be registered in the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS). RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed managing general partner and [Name] is appointed as AML compliance officer and authorised signatory. RESOLVED, that the managing general partner and the appointed registered agent are authorised to execute deliverables, file the RCS/UBO registrations, open bank accounts and engage the company secretary, and to do all acts necessary to give full effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed name and legal form 'SCSp' through the LBR online portal. Verify absence of identical or confusingly similar names registered in the RCS and confirm the name includes an appropriate distinction from existing legal persons. Obtain a name availability decision or reservation certificate before preparing the constitutional documents.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership deed or covering letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to similarity, submit a modified name with one or two fallback alternatives within 2 business days through the same portal; the first resubmission is accepted without additional state filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the SCSp partnership deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the partnership deed containing identity of the general partner and initial limited partner, registered office, corporate purpose, capital contributions, profit and loss allocation, management provisions, and dissolution terms. Execute the deed before a Luxembourg notary when required by investor commitments, property contributions, or regulatory preference; otherwise execute as a private written deed signed by all partners.
required_dossiers: Passports or identity cards of all partners
Professional biographies of general partner managers
Tax residence certificates of partners where available
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or counsel queries a provision, revise the deed by private addendum or notarial modification and obtain re-execution; pre-clearance of the draft with the notary mitigates notary-driven delays.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of bank account and collection of capital contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or professional of the financial sector
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an operating or escrow account in the name of the future SCSp with a Luxembourg bank. Transfer initial cash capital, or document in-kind contributions, in accordance with the contribution schedule in the partnership deed. Obtain the bank's account opening certificate and, if applicable, a blocked-funds confirmation. No statutory minimum capital is required.
required_dossiers: Passports and evidence of identity of partners
Source of funds and source of wealth statements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises AML concerns, provide supplemental source-of-wealth documentation and an explanation of the commercial purpose; if the bank declines based on internal risk appetite, select an alternative Luxembourg credit institution without delaying the RCS filing more than 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation documents with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed partnership deed, the RCS registration application form, registered office consent, and identity documents. Pay the RCS registration fee. Upon approval, receive the RCS registration number, official extract, and statutory filing receipt. The SCSp acquires commercial registration as of the filing date.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of signed partnership deed
Copy of registered office address authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues an incompleteness letter, cure within 15 calendar days by filing amended or supplemental documents through the LBR portal; a complete resubmission avoids refusal and preserves the original priority date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic publication in the RESA official gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS / Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, the RCS arranges the publication of the partnership deed or an extract in RESA in accordance with Luxembourg law. Verify the publication text, legal form, capital, registered office, and partners.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication contains errors, submit a corrected amendment deed and a request to the RCS within 5 business days to issue a rectified publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of ultimate beneficial owners in the UBO register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) via Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Identify all natural persons ultimately owning or controlling 25% or more of the SCSp, including through the general partner or limited partners. File the UBO declaration electronically with the LBR within one month of incorporation and pay the prescribed filing fee.
required_dossiers: Partnership deed extract showing control rights
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UBO filing is queried, file a correction within 5 business days; where the statutory deadline was missed, submit a justified late-filing request with supporting chronology to avoid or mitigate administrative fines.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Luxembourg VAT and direct tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA; Administration des contributions directes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp for Luxembourg VAT if it will perform taxable registered-agent or secretarial services. Complete the registration forms, indicate the intended business activity, and obtain a VAT number. Notify the direct tax administration and register for municipal corporate income tax and net wealth tax applicable to fiscally transparent partnerships at member level.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax administration requests clarification, provide a precise breakdown of taxable versus exempt services and amend the registration within 10 business days; late VAT registration is cured by immediate filing and voluntary payment of any sheltered VAT.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Regulatory licensing and AML registration as registered agent and company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and/or Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing the regulated activity of domiciliation, registered agency, or company secretarial services, file the application for authorization or registration as a trust and company service provider. Submit the programme of operations, AML/CFT policies, organizational chart, fitness and propriety evidence, and internal governance arrangements. Do not provide regulated services before the authorization or registration is effective.
required_dossiers: Licence application to CSSF or Ministry of Justice
Organizational chart and internal governance arrangements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the regulator raises a deficiency, respond to the information request within 10 business days with revised policies or an updated programme of operations; resubmission does not start a new review where the original file remains open.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for trust and company service provider licensing; Ministry of Justice for domiciliation agent authorization; Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) for occupational safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registered Agent and Company Secretarial Services Licence, including trust and company service provider (TCSP) registration and domiciliation agent authorization under Luxembourg law

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement, Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Category C - non-industrial office use; no mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment for registered-agent and secretarial activity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams; sanitary effluents must comply with municipal sewage bylaws and EU Urban Waste Water Treatment Directive 91/271/EEC; general waste must be handled by approved operators under the Luxembourg Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Direction de la Sécurité en Incendie et sur les Chantiers; municipal building structural load inspection for the registered office; occupational workplace clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), including first-aid, evacuation, and emergency response plans.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); euro-area monetary policy and TARGET2 clearing are administered by the European Central Bank (ECB), and prudential banking and professional gatekeeper supervision is delegated to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area member with full and unrestricted euro convertibility over both current and capital accounts; no exchange-control permit, capital-export licence, central bank approval or repatriation quota exists because cross-border capital movements are liberalised under Article 63 TFEU and Regulation (EC) No 924/2009. The Luxembourg SCSp may freely receive capital contributions, disburse trade payments and remit profits and distributions abroad, subject only to bank-level AML/FATF screening, RBE beneficial-ownership disclosure and BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting thresholds. Profit and dividend remittances face no conversion hurdle because the euro is fully deliverable, and distributions from a fiscally transparent SCSp are generally not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable in Luxembourg: neither the BCL, the CSSF nor the ECB imposes any statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio or surrender obligation on export receipts or service-rendering proceeds. The registered agent and secretarial firm may retain and settle fees in EUR or any freely traded currency via TARGET2/EURO1 or correspondent bank rails; only the ECB balance-of-payments and international investment position reporting obligation, collected by the BCL, applies to cross-border flows above the de minimis reporting threshold.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR current and correspondent clearing ledger)
Capital Escrow Account with segregated client-money ledger

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to medium: a Luxembourg-licensed payment institution or electronic-money institution under the Law of 10 November 2009 and CSSF supervision can support low-value client fee collection, but tier-1 Luxembourg banks generally refuse an offshore or post-Brexit UK/Malta/Lithuania EMI as the principal clearing account of an SCSp without a Luxembourg substance footprint. Purely digital onboarding of a partnership without a mandatory professional agent certificate is effectively not offered; the SCSp should therefore rely on BCL-member direct clearing rails rather than sub-threshold EMI rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the amended Law of 12 November 2004 on AML/CFT and CSSF guidance, the onboarding bank must identify the SCSp, its general partner, every authorised signatory and each limited partner holding more than 25% or acting as de facto controller, using reliable independent documentation. A physical or live video interview of the general partner's managing director is the customary bank standard, and for non-EU directors a face-to-face interview at the Luxembourg branch, a notarially certified corporate extract and a legal opinion from a Luxembourg avocat are required; purely remote opening without any Luxembourg registered agent is generally not viable at tier-1 institutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp constituted without legal personality; bank uncertainty over the identity of the contracting and liable party
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership agreement, current RCS extract naming the general partner, written confirmation that the partnership acts through its general partner, power of attorney for signatories, Luxembourg legal opinion, RBE receipt and bank-specific beneficial-ownership questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Zero minimum capital and pass-through tax status raising substance and profit-shifting red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements or a comfort letter from a réviseur d'entreprises agréé, substance file covering the physical registered office, local management minutes, client contracts and fee invoices, tax opinion confirming pass-through classification and the commercial rationale for each capital flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee or corporate limited partners creating beneficial-ownership opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed RBE declaration and receipt from the Registre de commerce, organisational chart of the full UBO chain, passport and proof of address of every natural-person UBO, and a certified copy of the limited partnership agreement demonstrating the economic share of each participating interest.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered agent and secretarial licence status under CSSF Circular 98/12 not evidenced, triggering gatekeeper-conduit risk on the Medium-Risk-Enhanced profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official agrément of the société d'administration de sociétés (company administration house) issued by the CSSF, professional indemnity insurance certificate, VAT and RCS excerpts, internal AML/CFT procedures manual and the declaration of appointment as statutory registered agent of the SCSp.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Limited-partner subscriptions and capital calls are executed by SEPA Credit Transfer within the EU or SWIFT MT103/202 for non-EU partners, credited to the SCSp EUR account over TARGET2 or EURO1 with next-business-day value under Regulation (EC) No 924/2009; the remittance must state the purpose narrative of capital contribution under the partnership agreement and be supported by the capital call notice, an extract of the limited partnership agreement and a source-of-wealth statement; USD, CHF and GBP legs are cleared through the Luxembourg bank's correspondent Nostro network, and flows above the statistical threshold are captured in the BCL balance-of-payments statement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade and operational disbursements settle via SWIFT MT103 single-payment transfers through the bank's correspondent network, including CHIPS in New York for USD, CHAPS for GBP and SIC for CHF; eurozone payments use SEPA Instant Credit Transfer up to EUR 100,000 or standard TARGET2/EURO1 clearing; documentary transactions are supported by commercial letters of credit issued by the Luxembourg account-holding bank under UCP600. Every disbursement above EUR 50,000 requires dual signature of the general partner and the registered agent, and the remitted fee must quote the applicable ISO 20022 purpose narrative so that BCL external-statistics compliance is met.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable EUR/USD forwards executed under an EMIR-compliant ISDA master agreement with a CSSF-authorised credit institution.
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps for economic hedging of EUR/USD, EUR/CHF and EUR/GBP trade flows, subject to EMIR clearing and margin thresholds.

European-style and barrier FX options purchased from a licensed Luxembourg or EU/EEA investment firm; writing of options is generally not permitted for the pass-through SCSp without specific professional authorisation.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only for illiquid third-country currency exposures where no deliverable market exists; for euro crosses they are unnecessary because the euro market is fully convertible and highly liquid.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (dépôt des comptes annuels au RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved within 6 months of the financial year-end and filed no later than one month after approval; hard deadline is 7 months after the balance sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 and publication of default; persistent non-filing after formal reminder can lead to court-ordered dissolution or strike-off of the SCSp from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (confirmation annuelle du registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and MyGuichet.lu
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for the preceding calendar year; any ownership transfer requires an updated RBE declaration within one month of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or confirm the UBO declaration is a criminal/administrative offence under Luxembourg AML law; fines may be imposed on the general partner and the SCSp, the default may be published, and continued non-compliance may block dealings and lead to deregistration

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatory for a small SCSp unless it is a regulated public-interest entity or AIF; audit becomes compulsory where the SCSp exceeds two of the three Luxembourg thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average workforce 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified in the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and Annual Accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU may be used for certain consolidated or regulated entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must file an annual RBE confirmation by 31 March even when no beneficial ownership has changed. If a limited partnership interest is transferred, the RBE declaration and RCS extract must be updated within one month; the transfer must also be recorded in the statutory register of limited partners before being opposable to third parties. The annual confirmation reconciles all transfers recorded as at the preceding 31 December.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors or Managing Partners

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,500 - USD 7,500 per annum depending on AML file maintenance and registered-office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 18,000 if audit becomes mandatory or is contractually required by investor documents

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0.00% at SCSp entity level (the Special Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent and has no legal personality; no Luxembourg corporate income tax is levied on the SCSp itself). Corporate partners are taxed at the combined Luxembourg headline CIT rate of 24.94% (17.00% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax in Luxembourg City, 2025 fiscal year); individual partners are taxed at progressive rates up to 45.78% in the income tax class 1.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Not applicable at the SCSp level because pass-through. At partner level, the following incentives may reduce the effective rate: participation exemption under Section 166 bis LIR (100% exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains where corporate partner holds >=10% or an acquisition cost of at least EUR 1,200,000 for 12 months); IP box regime (80% exemption of qualifying net IP income, effective rate approximately 5.18%); notional interest deduction (NID) on qualifying net equity increases at the annual rate published by the Luxembourg tax administration; 20% super-deduction on qualifying wage costs; no subscription tax (taxe d'abonnement) applies because the SCSp in this scope is a commercial service vehicle rather than a regulated investment fund.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 510 (Déclaration pour l'impôt commercial communal) - municipal business tax return; filed annually via the Luxembourg direct tax e-filing portal (Espace professionnel of the Administration des contributions directes, accessible through MyGuichet.lu) at the bureau d'imposition des sociétés of the SCSp's registered office.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end; the statutory deadline is automatically extended to 31 December where the return is filed electronically by a registered Luxembourg tax adviser (standard administrative practice).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RCS registration number, legal form code (SCSp), registered office address, general partner (commandité) identification, fiscal year end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the full name, address, and Luxembourg tax file number (numéro d'identification fiscale) of the SCSp; non-resident partners do not file on this box but are identified in the transparency annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial taxable profit or loss of the SCSp from the registered-agent and secretarial activity before allocation, after statutory depreciation and the municipal business tax allowance (franchise d'assiette).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The taxable result is computed at the enterprise level; the tax-base allowance is applied at partnership level and the net amount is then allocated to the partners according to the partnership agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Répartition du résultat entre associés
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of the taxable result per partner: name, tax residence, profit participation ratio, allocated profit or loss amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners are taxable in Luxembourg only on the profit share attributable to the Luxembourg permanent establishment (the registered office through which the services are rendered); they must file a non-resident corporate or individual return (Form 500/Form 100) via a Luxembourg fiscal representative where taxable thresholds are met. No Luxembourg withholding tax is levied on the distribution of the allocated share.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% surcharge (majoration d'impôt) on the tax assessed under Article 171 LIR plus late-payment interest of 0.6% per month (Article 155 LIR). Non-filing after formal notice: ex officio assessment (imposition d'office) with an additional surcharge of up to 25% of the tax evaded (concealment penalty, Article 174 LIR).
